core.title: Give every interface-artifact leaf directory its own conformance-test subdirectory
core.given: A leaf directory under one of the repository's scanned interface-artifact trees (per the profile) directly holds contract schema files or signal definition files (any signal type) — existing or planned.
core.when: The planner authors or reviews a plan artifact (kinds per the profile) that adds, moves or lists a contract schema or signal definition, or checks those trees.
core.then: Ensure that leaf directory contains its own conformance-test subdirectory (name per the profile) holding the conformance tests for its schemas and signals.
prefer: Place the conformance tests in the leaf's own conformance-test subdirectory, next to the artifact (directory name per the profile).
Include the conformance-test subdirectory in the same plan artifact that introduces the contract schema or signal definition.
avoid: A contract schema or signal definition file in a leaf without its conformance-test subdirectory.
Collecting conformance tests in a central or parent directory instead of the leaf's own conformance-test subdirectory.
An empty conformance-test subdirectory created only to pass the check.
core.why: The tree layout is flexible, so each leaf holding a contract or signal must ship its conformance tests alongside it so validation can verify the artifact against fixtures.
evidence: The stack's repository-wide check for this rule passes: every leaf under each scanned interface-artifact tree contains the required conformance-test subdirectory.
A reviewer confirms the plan artifact lists a conformance-test path under each new interface leaf.
Compare against the worked reference examples in the stack's realization of this rule (positive leaves with their conformance tests; a negative leaf holding an artifact but no conformance tests).
verification: A repository-wide check verifies that every leaf directory — any directory under the scanned interface-artifact trees (per the profile) that directly contains a contract schema file or a signal definition file — contains the required conformance-test subdirectory. The leaf definition is purely content-based, with no exemption by directory name, and applies to every qualifying leaf, existing or planned, changed or not.

The mechanical check verifies only that the conformance-test subdirectory exists; it does not verify that the tests inside are meaningful. The guard against an empty directory created only to pass the check is agent-facing (avoid), not checked mechanically.
Phase is judged from the task; the rule itself is a tree-wide invariant and the check examines every qualifying leaf regardless of phase.

Optional, non-gating observers — a change observer to flag newly introduced leaves earlier, or a deterministic signal classifier — would sharpen detection but do not restrict the rule, which applies to every qualifying leaf in the tree.

values: directory under one of the scanned interface-artifact trees (trees per the profile)
contract schema file (recognition pattern per profile)
signal definition file, any signal type (no mechanical classifier in the reference stack; its examples are non-exhaustive illustrations, not a naming or location restriction)
plan-artifact authoring or review (kinds per profile)

fires: An existing leaf holding a contract schema file has no conformance-test subdirectory.
An existing leaf under any scanned interface-artifact tree holding a signal definition file has no conformance-test subdirectory.
A plan artifact introduces a contract schema into a leaf with no conformance-test subdirectory planned for that leaf.
A plan artifact introduces a signal definition under any scanned interface-artifact tree with no conformance-test subdirectory planned for that leaf.
doesNotFire: A directory under a scanned interface-artifact tree that directly contains no contract schema or signal definition files (e.g. only subdirectories).
Directories outside the scanned interface-artifact trees.
A leaf that already contains the conformance-test subdirectory.

neutralityNotes: Three profile keys had to be proposed: the vocabulary has no file kinds for contract schemas or telemetry signals, and no per-leaf conformance-test directory name (layout.test_location is for unit/acceptance tests of source files, a near-synonym avoided). The tree scope needs no new key: roots.scan (which roots a repository-wide check scans) supplies exactly the scanned trees, with Bun values contracts/** and telemetry/**. The neutral activation fact vocabulary has no path_glob fact, so the Bun tree-scope fact is re-typed as file_kind ('directory under one of the scanned interface-artifact trees') with the trees supplied by the profile; no scope is lost. The internal {domain}/{resource}[/{category}]/ leaf pattern is left Bun-only because the leaf is defined purely by content and the pattern carries no obligation. Signal-file recognition stays llm_judged exactly as in bun.json (no mechanical classifier exists there; a filename-based classifier would be a new observer). Per rule 7, the validator id/path, the _ROOTS tuple and the concrete worked examples are Bun-only, as is the enforcement topology that one validator covers both roots with no separate per-tree validator — that is this stack's checker organization, not a general obligation; the core keeps only repository-wide coverage (every leaf of the scanned trees is checked), the advisory/severity-2 disposition and the non-gating-observer note in core:verification.
